component_and_cause.primary: A thick left crown bridges a shifted, irregular opening to a narrower right support.
secondary: Two weaker beds recede through depth and support width.
A planar shoulder joint removes a broad front-left corner.
The back-right shoulder is thinner than its front.
component_and_cause.tertiary: The removed shoulder fragment lies locally below its source; one smaller chip shares the fall zone.
component_and_cause.quiet_region: The resistant upper crown retains broad unbroken facets.

budget_profile.role: Single focal geological landmark and close gallery inspection; not a repeated background rock.
budget_profile.lod: One close/medium mesh in this sample. No distant LOD or performance claim.
budget_profile.reason: Geometry is reserved for broad undercuts, the shoulder fracture, depth variation, and the opening; no subdivision is added merely to approach a ceiling.
budget_profile.unverified: Target-device frame times, 8-instance scene timing and 32px distant suitability remain unmeasured.

reference_learning.principle: Middle-scale, cause-based structure remains visible after color removal.
reference_learning.reuse: No RHS059 model, code, palette, texture, or screenshot is incorporated.

scientific_scope.en: Original stylized erosion-landform concept; not a reconstructed named arch, fossil locality, or geological measurement.
scientific_scope.zh: 原创风格化侵蚀地貌概念，不对应具体石拱、化石地点或地质测量。

design_notes: Bedding shifts both surface position and support thickness; bands alone no longer provide the entire geological story.
The detached flake is the actual cut piece, not an evenly distributed decorative pebble.
All geometry is original and deterministic.
